name: Mitochondrial Disease with Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Mitochondrial Disease Diagnostic Criteria with Cardiomyopathy Features

criteria.description: Presence of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy confirmed by echocardiography or cardiac MRI
Biochemical evidence of mitochondrial respiratory chain dysfunction in muscle biopsy or fibroblasts
Identification of pathogenic mitochondrial DNA or nuclear DNA mutations associated with mitochondrial disease
Presence of neurological symptoms such as muscle weakness or exercise intolerance
Elevated blood or CSF lactate levels indicating mitochondrial metabolic impairment

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy plus biochemical or genetic evidence of mitochondrial dysfunction
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, biochemical, and genetic data due to phenotypic heterogeneity.

pathognomonic.notes: Concentric left ventricular hypertrophy without other causes

pathognomonic.symptomName: Exercise intolerance due to mitochondrial myopathy
pathognomonic.notes: Reduced muscle endurance related to mitochondrial dysfunction
searchTerms: poor exercise tolerance from muscle mitochondrial disease
fatigue during physical activity due to myopathy

pathognomonic.symptomName: Elevated blood lactate levels at rest or post-exercise
searchTerms: high blood lactate at rest or after exercise
elevated lactic acid levels in blood

common.notes: Symmetric weakness affecting limb girdle muscles
searchTerms: weakness mainly in upper arms and thighs
muscle weakness close to body center
irregular heartbeats including fast ventricular rhythm

common.symptomName: Neuropathic symptoms such as peripheral neuropathy
searchTerms: tingling or burning in hands and feet

occasional.notes: Due to mitochondrial involvement of cochlear cells

occasional.symptomName: Diabetes mellitus secondary to mitochondrial endocrine dysfunction
searchTerms: diabetes caused by mitochondrial endocrine problems
drooping eyelids and eye muscle weakness

laboratory: Elevated blood and CSF lactate and pyruvate levels
Elevated creatine kinase in some cases
Abnormal mitochondrial respiratory chain enzyme activities in muscle biopsy
imaging: Echocardiography showing concentric left ventricular hypertrophy
Cardiac MRI demonstrating myocardial fibrosis and hypertrophy
Brain MRI may show stroke-like lesions or basal ganglia abnormalities
genetic: Pathogenic variants in mitochondrial DNA genes (e.g., MT-TL1, MT-ND genes)
Nuclear gene mutations affecting mitochondrial function (e.g., MYH7, TAZ)
Heteroplasmy levels correlating with disease severity
other: Muscle biopsy showing ragged-red fibers and abnormal mitochondrial morphology

distinguishingFeatures: Genetic mutations typically in sarcomeric proteins
Lack of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy on imaging
Predominant neurological or muscular symptoms without cardiac involvement

redFlags: Rapid progression of cardiac hypertrophy with arrhythmias
Early onset multisystem involvement including neurological decline
references: DiMauro S, Schon EA. Mitochondrial respiratory-chain diseases. N Engl J Med. 2003 Jun 19;348(26):2656-68.
Finsterer J. Mitochondrial disorders, cognitive impairment and dementia. J Neurol Sci. 2012 Sep 15;318(1-2):1-5.
